title: Data and normalizations for finite-span module comparisons
statement: For a prime l, nativeAb is the native locally finite-function abelian sheaf, ring is its reconstructed section ring, and internal is the category of internal modules over the pulled-back condensed coefficient. For a ring isomorphism theta, equivalence is restriction along theta inverse followed by the fixed sectionModuleEquivalence. The ordinary direct and inverse images are the ringed-site pushforward and sheafified tensor pullback. Data stores these specified coefficient maps, ordinary comparisons, exactness and derived comparison; Properties is the original seventeen-clause normalization predicate, and ExchangeProperty is the original comparison of the specified exchange maps. The original declarations retain their signatures, attributes and mathematical definitions; no new mathematical object is selected. The field-normalization and exchange formulas are factored as DerivedNormalization and ExchangeEquation before their field binders; the formulas and every binder are retained. The two canonical derived adjunctions are shared abbreviations, used by the exchange and normalization formulas, with their original defining expressions. DerivedComparisonFrame and derivedComparisonFrame bundle the same canonical categories, functors, compositors, comparisons and adjunctions. The mate-normalization and exchange formulas use projections of this one bundle, without changing their expanded formulas; the exchange object binder uses its literal internal derived category field. MateCondition and ExchangeCondition state the two equations over an abstract bundle, so their concrete specializations keep its exact category instances. Frame projection instances are local to elaboration and introduce no exported instance attributes. PullbackExchangeCondition extracts the commutative square at an abstract bundle; ExchangeEquation specializes this wrapper on the original pullback square. This moves no hypothesis and changes no equation. The bundle is universe-specialized to its actual derived category sizes: object universe u+2 and morphism universe u+1; only the scheme universe u is a parameter.
